reason: Conversation 1 asked the two most useful questions (RCD vs MCB, hot vs cold programme), correctly explained the heater-linked earth-leakage pattern, noted the insulation test is an engineer job, correctly identified that the heater is integrated into the circulation pump on this Electrolux-group machine, and told the homeowner not to keep resetting and to keep it unplugged. Its weaknesses were saying the pattern 'pretty much confirms' the element without testing, being soft about allowing cold rinses, and suggesting tilting the machine to look underneath. Conversation 2 led with a firm and appropriate stop-using warning, but then misread the facts and issued a 'water near the plug or socket is dangerous' alert after the homeowner had just said the floor and socket were dry, asked no useful diagnostic questions, and gave no part guidance or explanation of why cold rinses never trip, making it less accurate and far less helpful despite its stronger safety tone.
